unlock_condition.description: Requires an open-sea capable ship — Cyprus is out of sight of the Phoenician coast

travel_note.description: First location that requires sailing out of sight of land. Triggers a unique moment when the coast disappears behind the player.

tile_details.description: reddish sandy soil — copper dust stains everything faintly orange
rougher and less organized than Tyre or Sidon — frontier feel
cart tracks worn into the dirt, ore dust coating all surfaces
white sand beach east of the port — fishing boats pulled up on shore

day.note: Brighter and hotter than the Phoenician coast

location.lore_note: Kition is a Phoenician colony but it does not feel purely Phoenician. Cypriots, Greeks, and Egyptians all trade here. The island is named after copper — and copper is everything here. The smelters never stop. It is rougher and more frontier than the Phoenician coast cities, with less law and more opportunity.

visual.description: A working port without much elegance. Three stone docks, a customs shed, sacks of ore waiting to load.

services.note: Best repair quality outside of Tyre — miners need their ships maintained well

visual.description: A large open building with a permanent smell of hot metal. Ingots stacked in rows by quality grade. Scales dominate every table. The floor is permanently stained orange.

inventory.note: Tin is not from Cyprus — it is imported from far west or north. Very profitable to bring here.

bulk_buy_mechanic.description: Buying 20+ copper ingots at once gives a 10% discount — encourages cargo-hold trading strategy

visual.description: The only tavern in Kition. Low ceiling, loud, constantly full of sailors from four different nations. Wine from three different places on the same table.

rumor_pool: A Greek sailor says there is a sunken ship full of bronze near the western reef
Someone claims pirates are using a cove on the north coast as a base
A Cypriot miner says they broke into a chamber in the mine that had things inside — old things
A merchant just arrived from Carthage says the price of ivory has doubled
rumor_mechanic.note: Kition rumors lean toward sea routes, piracy, and distant price changes — reflecting its frontier character

visual.description: A functional mud-brick building at the start of the mine road. Maps of the mine on the walls. Ore samples on every surface.

services.description: Allows player to enter the mine area. Required for mine-related quests.

lines.speaker: abdimilk
lines.text: Copper or bronze? Raw or refined? How much weight can your ship carry? Answer those three questions and we can do business.

player_choices.text: Where do you get your tin from?

lines.speaker: abdimilk
lines.text: Tin. That's the problem. We have all the copper on the island but we import every bar of tin from far away. Supply is unreliable. If you can bring me regular tin shipments — we talk serious money.

lines.speaker: nikodemos
lines.text: A Phoenician! You people own half the sea. No offense. I mean that as a compliment.

lines.speaker: nikodemos
lines.text: I've been to places your maps don't show. Buy me wine and I'll tell you about them.

lines.speaker: nikodemos
lines.text: I sailed north once. Past Greece, past the islands. There are islands up there covered in fog and full of tin. The people there paint themselves blue. Strange place.

lines.speaker: nikodemos
lines.text: I also heard — from a man who heard it from another man — that someone sailed west past the Pillars and found land. Green land. Not a story. A fact.

entry_position.description: Deep inside the copper mine, past the active shafts — a collapsed section leads to a sealed chamber

discovery_triggers.description: Foreman mentions a collapse that exposed something old

contents.description: A pre-Phoenician chamber inside the mine. Walls carved with offerings to a copper deity. Bronze objects arranged in ritual patterns on the floor.
Ship carvings — same unknown ship design as Tyre's Drowned Quarter and Byblos temple. Three locations, same mysterious ships.

reward_summary.note: Third sighting of the mysterious ship carvings — the player now has enough evidence to ask Shipitbaal in Byblos about the unknown civilization

steps.description: Find a reliable source of tin — Tartessos or the northern route via Greek contacts

steps.note: Unlocks Tartessos route hint if player has not been there yet

reward.description: Establishes a recurring tin contract — every time player brings 10+ tin ingots to Kition, they receive bonus silver above market price

options.description: Pocket the bronze figurines and say nothing

steps.description: Get the approximate reef location from Nikodemos
Sail to the western reef near Kition

options.description: Sell salvaged bronze to Abdimilk at the copper exchange
Keep and sell in a city where bronze is more valuable

reward.note: Pure profit from salvage — no purchase cost. Teaches diving mechanic.

economy.note: Kition is the copper source for the entire game. Buy copper here, sell everywhere else. The tin arbitrage is the main money-making mechanic here.
